searchText: I actually support a BASEFEE opcode! > I actually support a BASEFEE opcode! <@273808422753796097> 👍 👍 👍 👍 <@273808422753796097> Why? Or do you just mean you don't see a problem with it? I don't see a problem, and I think it's actively useful eg. imagine payment channels or plasma chains delaying withdrawal periods if the base fee is higher or any application that involves compensating someone the tx fees they use to send some message That feels prone to working today and not tomorrow. It was *insane* to think gas prices would get to 500+ and stay there were months ago. To the point that Geth had a hard cap in code! wait how? adding a BASEFEE opcode in code makes it *easier* to build incentives that are more robust to wide swings in gasprices Because the contract can know what those swings are in real time But it requires either governance to manage what "high" means, or it requires hard coding something that will be wrong eventually. why does it require governance? so here is a really simple example imagine a contract that needs to get poked Because we cannot define "high" at a single point in time and have it remain accurate indefinitely. It can provide an incentive for the poke that's equal to basefee + N gwei where N could grow over time for added robustness I think this is only possible with gas cost observability, which we want to get rid of? I suppose it works for short term things. anything where you can frequently feed in the gas cost as an outside input which channels are one example of actually Where I put something out there that will compensate before the next hard fork (when gas costs change). right, or that Okay, I'm convinced that it is reasonable for short term repayment/compensation commitments. Though, I worry that people will use it for long term stuff (e.g., hard code it into contracts). I suppose we can't stop everyone from shooting themselves in the foot... I just wish we were more willing to burn those people with gas cost changes. (I think we are getting better) Personally I want 2929 to go in without 2930 just as a stake in the ground saying "yes, we are willing to make occasional tough choices" 😆
